13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or -5- body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence.

22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
24. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance.
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc.

Exploitation as referred to in Article 3 letter e is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, thus requiring legal protection to protect their honor and dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".
The Regional Government is obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilitation for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in Konawe Kepulauan Regency.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, thus requiring legal protection to protect their honor and dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".
The Regional Government is obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilitation for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in Konawe Kepulauan Regency.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, thus requiring legal protection to protect their honor and dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".
The Regional Government is obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilitation for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in Konawe Kepulauan Regency.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, thus requiring legal protection to protect their honor and dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".
The Regional Government is obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilitation for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in Konawe Kepulauan Regency.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, thus requiring legal protection to protect their honor and dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".
The Regional Government is obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilitation for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in Konawe Kepulauan Regency.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, thus requiring legal protection to protect their honor and dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".
The Regional Government is obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilitation for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in Konawe Kepulauan Regency.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, thus requiring legal protection to protect their honor and dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".
The Regional Government is obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilitation for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in Konawe Kepulauan Regency.

Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. The Regional Government is obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilitation for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or -5- body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
19. Services are immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for strengthening victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to family or community who can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
24. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance.
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc.
26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Every citizen has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from all forms of violence. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, thus requiring legal protection to protect their honor and dignity and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
This view is based on Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right".
The Regional Government is obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring -2- the implementation of service facilitation for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Konawe Kepulauan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in Konawe Kepulauan Regency.
